text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambia press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Agriculture minister Edith Nawakwi says 200 jobs will be created at the newly commissioned Finta Dannish Dairies milk processing plant in the southern town of Livingstone.
- The Zambia National Farmers Union commends the Reserve Food Agency for securing 120,000 tonnes of maize from neighbouring Zimbabwe to replenish depleting stocks.
- The Zambia Telephone Corp urges the government to ban the export of scrap metal to curb the increasing theft of telephone cables.

- The supreme court is to decide on Wednesday whether to subject president Frederick Chiluba to a DNA test to establish his parentage. Opposition leaders challenging his credentials say the president lied about his parentage and nationality in filing election nomination papers.
- The African Development Bank says it will allocate $32 million towards the rehabilitation of the water system in the mining town of Kitwe.
- Agriculture minister Edith Nawakwi warns that donors will soon start dictating to Zambians on how to dress if the country does not reduce its dependence on external aid.
